hints: Interpret the three conditions as regions on the Argand diagram and take their intersection.
Draw the closed disc centred at the origin with radius $3$, and the vertical boundary $\operatorname{Re}z=-2$ with the side to its right.
Draw the rays with arguments $\pi/4$ and $\pi$, then shade only the part of the disc lying to the right of $x=-2$ and within that angular sector; all boundaries are included.
walkthrough:
Identify the geometric locus represented by $|z| \leq 3$:
The boundary $|z| = 3$ represents a circle with centre at the origin $(0, 0)$ and radius $3$.
The inequality $|z| \leq 3$ defines the closed disk containing all points on and inside this circle.

Identify the geometric locus represented by $\operatorname{Re} z \geq -2$:
Writing $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$, the real part is $\operatorname{Re} z = x$.
The equation $x = -2$ represents a vertical straight line cutting the real axis at $(-2, 0)$, to the right of the circle's leftmost point $(-3, 0)$.
The inequality $x \geq -2$ represents the region on and to the right of this vertical line.

Identify the angular sector defined by $\dfrac{1}{4}\pi \leq \arg z \leq \pi$:
The half-line $\arg z = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$ starts from the origin and extends into the first quadrant along the line $y = x$ ($x > 0, y > 0$).
The half-line $\arg z = \pi$ represents the negative real axis ($x < 0, y = 0$).
The inequality includes all complex numbers whose argument lies between these two rays, sweeping counterclockwise across the upper portion of the first quadrant and the entire second quadrant.

Combine the three conditions to shade the region of intersection:
1. Inside or on the circular boundary of radius $3$ centered at the origin.
2. On or to the right of the solid vertical line $x = -2$.
3. Between the solid ray $\arg z = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$ and the solid negative real axis $\arg z = \pi$.
